key_insight: Individually safe ASR and note-generation components can still combine into meaningful clinical risk at the final note stage, especially across complex or low-resource language settings.
clinical_relevance: For ambient AI scribes, safety should be assessed on the clinician-facing note, not just transcription accuracy, because interface errors can amplify harm.
method: Two-arm evaluation on a common clinical-risk scale using a frozen synthetic corpus
Compared intrinsic generation (reference script→note) with end-to-end generation (ASR transcript→note)
Three LLM raters labeled discrepancies with a four-mode error taxonomy across 77 languages and five complexity levels
evidence_signal: Serious-note errors were low in intrinsic generation (3.4%) but rose sharply end-to-end with complexity and language scarcity, with 87% of serious errors attributed to ASR-derived issues.
watch_item: Because the study used scripted synthetic consultations and LLM-based raters, real-world performance and error patterns may differ from deployed clinical workflows.
paper_title: Mind the gap: emergent clinical risk at the interface of two individually safe AI systems in a multilingual ambient scribe
